rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Seeking permission is obligatory: it protects the person visited from unwelcome intrusion, dispute, insults, harsh speech, and grounds for suspicion.
rows.anchor: فائدة الاستئذان دفع ما يكره عن المطروق المزور وقطع أسباب الإنكار أو الشتم أو الإغلاظ في القول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Greeting alongside permission strengthens established affection; that purpose makes greeting emphatically recommended, not obligatory.
rows.anchor: فائدة السلام مع الاستئذان فهي تقوية الألفة المتقررة فلا تقتضي أكثر من تأكد الاستحباب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an gives the complete form of proper conduct while the Sunnah explains its component rulings, as in the Qur'an's stated role of clarification.
rows.anchor: فالقرآن أمر بالحالة الكاملة وأحال تفصيل أجزائها على تبيين السنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse summarizes the wisdom of permission: it brings benefit, which people are expected to recognize through reflection.
rows.anchor: أي ذلكم الاستئذان خير لكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The coordinating conjunction requires both courtesies but sets no order; either order fulfills the request, though reports prescribing greeting first make that order preferable.
rows.anchor: جمعت الآية الاستئذان والسلام بواو العطف المفيد التشريك فقط فدلت على أنه إن قدم الاستئذان على السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Permission has no fixed formula; phrases found in reports reflect customary speech or a more concise way to express the purpose.
rows.anchor: فإنما محمله على أنه المتعارف بينهم أو على أنه كلام أجمع من غيره في المراد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A visitor who receives no permission repeats the request three times, then leaves.
rows.anchor: أن المستأذن إن لم يؤذن له بالدخول يكرره ثلاث مرات فإذا لم يؤذن له انصرف

rows.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
rows.claim: A report in Sahih al-Bukhari has Abu Musa cite the Prophet's rule to return after three unanswered requests; Umar asks for corroboration, Ubay sends the youngest witness, Abu Sa'id, and Umar says market business had distracted him from the report.
rows.anchor: كنت في مجلس من مجالس الأنصار إذ جاء أبو موسى الأشعري

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This scene adds abuse delivered when the disbelievers see the Prophet to the earlier insults they made in his absence.
rows.anchor: فعطف عليها في هذه الآية أذى خاص وهو الأذى حين يرونه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They ridicule him because his modest dress, manner, companions, and care for the weak do not resemble the status and leadership they expect of God's messenger.
rows.anchor: مشاهدة الرسول في غير زي الكبراء والمترفين لا يجر المطارف ولا يركب النجائب ولا يمشي مرحا

rows.speaker: أبو جهل وأهل ناديه
rows.claim: Ibn Ashur identifies Abu Jahl and the people in his assembly as the speakers of this mocking remark.
rows.anchor: وهذا الكلام صدر من أبي جهل وأهل ناديه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: إذا is a temporal expression carrying conditional force, so the following clause إن يتخذونك إلا هزؤا functions as its response.
rows.anchor: مضمن معنى الشرط فلذلك يجعل متعلقه جوابا له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: هزؤ is the verbal noun of هزأ به; Ibn Ashur points to the earlier Qur'anic usage in 2:67.
rows.anchor: قالوا أتتخذنا هزوءا } في سورة البقرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling him ridicule itself intensifies the mockery: they devote him wholly to being mocked.
rows.anchor: والوصف للمبالغة في استهزائهم به حتى كأنه نفس الهزؤ لأنهم محضوه لذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plural subject shows that groups mock the Prophet when they see him in their gatherings and meeting places.
rows.anchor: للدلالة على أن جماعاتهم يستهزئون به إذا رأوه وهم في مجالسهم ومنتدياتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The restrictive exception is from the range of denied states: they persist in mocking him and never mix it with reflection on his words or call.
rows.anchor: يلازمونه ويدأبون عليه ولا يخلطون معه شيئا من تذكر أقواله ودعوته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their quoted question explains the mockery because the ridicule takes the form of speech exchanged among them.
rows.anchor: لأن الاستهزاء من قبيل القول فكان بيانه بما هو من أقوالهم ومجاذبتهم الأحاديث بينهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question denies that God sent him as a messenger, while the demonstrative signals contempt and belittlement.
rows.anchor: اسم الإشارة مستعمل في الاستصغار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse consoles the Prophet over repeated rejection despite his eagerness to guide them: people who make desire their deity are not expected to find guidance.
rows.anchor: استئناف خوطب به الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم فيما يخطر بنفسه من الحزن على تكرر إعراضهم عن دعوته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: اتخذ takes two objects as a causative verb, closer to كسا and أعطى than to ظن; the first object is transformed into the state named by the second.
rows.anchor: إلى باب كسا وأعطى أقرب منه إلى باب ظن

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: On the unadvanced object order, a person makes the thing he desires to worship his deity; idolaters worship idols from appetite rather than proof of their right to worship.
rows.anchor: ومعناه منقول عن سعيد بن جبير

rows.speaker: ابن عرفة
rows.claim: Ibn Arfa chose the ordinary-order interpretation as the sole correct one; Ibn Ashur says his categorical judgment is not convincing.
rows.anchor: واختاره ابن عرفة في ( تفسيره )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With the second object advanced, the person makes desire his guide, acting only in accord with appetite; desire is then like a deity through his obedience to it.
rows.anchor: من اتخذ هواه قدوة له في أعماله لا يأتي عملا إلا إذا كان وفاقا لشهوته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the advanced-object reading, calling desire a deity is an emphatic metaphor: it resembles a god in the obedience it receives.
rows.anchor: شبيها بإلهه في إطاعته على طريقة التشبيه البليغ

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas is associated with the broader reading that a person follows desire as a deity; it condemns idolatry and other wrongs and indecencies.
rows.anchor: أفعالهم . ونحا إليه ابن عباس

rows.speaker: صاحب الكشاف وابن عطية
rows.claim: Al-Kashshaf's author and Ibn Atiyya also adopt the broader reading of following desire as a deity.
rows.anchor: ذهب صاحب ( الكشاف ) وابن عطية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Both object-order interpretations should be understood as intended meanings of the verse.
rows.anchor: وكلا المعنيين ينبغي أن يكون محملا للآية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the two clauses form one connected construction, رأيت means cognitive knowledge, the first question is rhetorical denial, and the second clause supplies the omitted second object.
rows.anchor: كلاما واحدا متصلا ثانيه بأوله اتصال المفعول بعامله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the connected construction, the interrogative suspends رأيت from taking its object; the second clause substitutes for that object, so one does not pause at هواه.
rows.anchor: الفعل معلق عن العمل فيه بسبب الاستفهام على نحو قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the connected reading, the first question gives an overview and the second elaborates it; the second interrogative reinforces the first, as in 17:49.
rows.anchor: على طريقة الإجمال ثم التفصيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, each clause is syntactically independent: the first question expresses astonished, mixed disapproval, and the فاء makes the second clause follow from it.
rows.anchor: مستعملا في التعجيب من حال الذين اتخذوا إلههم هواهم تعجيبا مشوبا بالإنكار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the independent-clause reading, the second question denies that the Prophet can pull someone out of error, continuing the point in 25:42.
rows.anchor: إنك لا تستطيع قلعه عن ضلاله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: من refers to the group described as seeing the punishment in 25:42; its attached pronouns remain singular by agreement with the word-form من.
rows.anchor: على الجمع المتحدث عنه في قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plural sense is either people who made desire a deity or people who took deities for the sake of desire; إله can be a generic singular for several gods.
rows.anchor: اتخذوا هواهم إلها لهم أو من اتخذوا آلهة لأجل هواهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Putting أنت before the verbal predicate emphasizes that the Prophet cannot serve as their keeper in a way that makes them believe by persistent calling.
rows.anchor: إشارة إلى إنكار ما حمل الرسول عليه الصلاة والسلام نفسه من الحرص والحزن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The point that the Prophet cannot compel people to believe parallels 10:99.
rows.anchor: أفأنت تكره الناس حتى يكونوا مؤمنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause كم أنبتنا is an appositive elaboration of يروا and carries the force of the rebuke; إلى الأرض depends on يروا.
rows.anchor: وقوله : { إلى الأرض } متعلق بفعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: كم is an exclamatory/interrogative-of-quantity expression used here as a nominal of abundance and as the object of أنبتنا: God grew many kinds.
rows.anchor: أنبتنا فيها كثيرا من كل زوج كريم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: من is partitive; the abundance of كم concerns growth in many places, while كل covers the kinds and varieties of plants, together pointing to fine design.
rows.anchor: هو كثرة الإنبات في أمكنة كثيرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The partitive phrasing makes it unnecessary to state an explicit classifier for كم, since the verse already mentions portions of each kind.
rows.anchor: واستغني بذكر أبعاض كل زوج عن ذكر مميز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: زوج means a kind or species and is commonly used for types outside the animal kingdom; compare the possible reading of 13:3 and the wording of 20:53.
rows.anchor: إطلاق الزوج على النوع في غير الحيوان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: كريم means precious or excellent within its kind; Ibn Ashur relates this usage to رزق كريم and مروا كراما.
rows.anchor: والكريم : النفيس من نوعه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The proof of God's craftsmanship also embeds a reminder of His favors: noble plants show the proof while adding the benefit of gratitude for blessings.
rows.anchor: وهذا من إدماج الامتنان في ضمن الاستدلال لأن الاستدلال على بديع الصنع يحصل بالنظر في إنبات الكريم وغيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People look more readily at desirable species because they seek their benefit and admire them; the verse uses what the polytheists already pursue as a reminder that leads to proof.
rows.anchor: طلب المنفعة منها والإعجاب بها فإذا تطلبها وقع في الاستدلال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: That refers to the earth, God's growth of the plant kinds, and the benefits and beauty those plants contain.
rows.anchor: وما في تلك الأزواج من منافع وبهجة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: إن treats the audience as if they denied that this growth and its qualities prove the oneness whose affirmation prompted their rejection of the Messenger.
rows.anchor: على ثبوت الوحدانية التي هي باعث تكذيبهم الرسول لما دعاهم إلى إثباتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: آية is singular either as a generic noun or distributively, since each of the several features mentioned constitutes a sign.
rows.anchor: لأن في المذكور عدة أشياء في كل واحد منها آية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The statement is attached to the clear proof and reports their persistence in disbelief; أكثرهم refers to the Meccan polytheists understood from context, as in 26:3.
rows.anchor: إخبارا عنهم بأنهم مصرون على الكفر بعد هذا الدليل الواضح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording says most rather than all because a few believed then or later.
rows.anchor: وأسند نفي الإيمان إلى أكثرهم لأن قليلا منهم يؤمنون حينئذ أو بعد ذلك

rows.speaker: سيبويه والمحققون
rows.claim: Sibawayh and the verifying grammarians treat كان here as an extra element used for emphasis.
rows.anchor: هنا مقحمة للتأكيد على رأي سيبويه والمحققين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This concluding statement appends God's power and mercy to the report about the unbelievers: His power could hasten punishment, while delay may mercifully lead them to gratitude.
rows.anchor: أي تمام القدرة فتعلمون أنه لو شاء لعجل لهم العقاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The description of God as merciful hints that He has mercy on the Messenger by supporting and aiding him.
rows.anchor: وفي وصف الرحمة إيماء إلى أنه يرحم رسله بتأييده ونصره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because this is a rational proof, Ibn Ashur says it is stated once; historical examples of earlier nations are repeated because they are a different kind of evidence.
rows.anchor: واعلم أن هذا الاستدلال لما كان عقليا اقتصر عليه ولم يكرر بغيره من نوع الأدلة العقلية كما كررت الدلائل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage begins examples confirming the Messenger through the fates of peoples who denied their messengers, warning the audience and recalling arguments delivered by earlier messengers.
rows.anchor: شروع في عد آيات على صدق الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم بذكر عواقب المكذبين برسلهم ليحذر المخاطبون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Several famous punishment histories are recounted rather than just one: recurrence weakens the possibility that a people's fate was accidental, since analogical evidence gains certainty through repetition and corroboration.
rows.anchor: لأن الدلالة غير العقلية يتطرقها احتمال عدم الملازمة بأن يكون ما أصاب قوما من أولئك على وجه الصدفة والاتفاق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses precedes Abraham out of the usual chronological order because the surah answers demands for supernatural signs: Pharaoh's defiance despite Moses' signs exemplifies the disbelievers' resistance.
rows.anchor: لعله لأن السورة نزلت للرد على المشركين في إلحاحهم على إظهار آيات من خوارق العادات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: إذ is a time noun governed by an omitted اذكر, as in the later instruction واتل عليهم نبأ إبراهيم; it also reminds and consoles the Messenger.
rows.anchor: اسم زمان منصوبا بفعل محذوف تقديره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's calling Moses means revelation through speech Moses heard directly, without an angel intermediary.
rows.anchor: ونداء الله موسى الوحي إليه بكلام سمعه من غير واسطة ملك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أن ائت is an explanatory clause clarifying what the call conveyed.
rows.anchor: و { أن } تفسيرية . والمقصود من سوق هذه القصة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The admonition's main point is the deniers' eventual fate at the sea; the preceding verses explain Moses' mission, Pharaoh's rejection, and what led to that ending.
rows.anchor: وذلك عند قوله تعالى : { فأوحينا إلى موسى أن اضرب بعصاك البحر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling them oppressors signals why Moses is sent, primes him to learn who they are, and stirs indignation to reinforce obedience and make his address more forceful; it hints their oppression is notorious.
rows.anchor: إيماء إلى علة الإرسال . وفي هذا الإجمال توجيه نفس موسى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Repeating قوم to specify Pharaoh's people adds emphasis; Ibn Ashur cites Jarir's repeated vocative يا تيم تيم عدي as a parallel.
rows.anchor: وفي تكرير كلمة { قوم } موقع من التأكيد فلم يقل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their oppression includes wronging themselves through idolatry and violating others' rights by enslaving and persecuting the Israelites.
rows.anchor: والظلم يعم أنواعه ، فمنها ظلمهم أنفسهم بعبادة ما لا يستحق العبادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an uses ظلم for both injustice against others and associationism against oneself, with examples at 2:114 and 6:82.
rows.anchor: وتقدم استعماله في المعنيين مرارا في ضد العدل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The account omits the opening call in 20:12–23 because this passage focuses on the mission to Pharaoh and his rejection; the Ta Ha account instead expands on Moses' honor and prophethood.
rows.anchor: قد عدل هنا عن ذكر ما ابتدىء به نداء موسى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command means Moses is to go and convey the message; the compressed wording is explained by the later command to go together to Pharaoh and speak.
rows.anchor: والإتيان المأمور به هو ذهابه لتبليغ الرسالة إليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On one parse, ألا consists of interrogative hamza plus negative لا; the question rejects the absence of fear and expresses Moses' astonishment.
rows.anchor: مركبا من حرفين همزة الاستفهام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As a standalone explanatory question, it shows their entrenched oppression and prepares Moses to persist despite their likely rejection; he knew their abuses from growing up among them.
rows.anchor: مستأنفة استئنافا بيانيا لأنه لما أمره بالإتيان إليهم لدعوتهم ووصفهم بالظالمين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second analysis takes ألا as one particle of urging, making the sentence an explanation of ائت: tell them, in effect, 'Will you not fear?'
rows.anchor: هي أداة العرض والتحضيض فتكون جملة : { ألا يتقون }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command can be reported by meaning rather than exact wording, as in the verse where Jesus describes what God commanded him to say.
rows.anchor: فحكى مقالته بمعناها لا بلفظها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fear and caution are the sense of اتقاء here; the implicit object is the consequences of their wrongdoing, as in the earlier usage in 8:56.
rows.anchor: والاتقاء : الخوف والحذر ، وحذف متعلق فعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The description of Pharaoh's people teaches Moses to begin by calling them away from injustice and toward piety.
rows.anchor: من إجراء وصف الظلم وعدم التقوى على قوم فرعون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Ashur points back to the mention of Moses at 2:51 and to the account of Pharaoh at 7:103.
rows.anchor: وذكر موسى تقدم عند قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The narrative omits Moses and Aaron going to Pharaoh, seeking entry, and delivering their message; Pharaoh addresses Moses as the principal messenger and treats Aaron as his aide.
rows.anchor: من الكلام ذهاب موسى وهارون إلى فرعون واستئذانهما عليه وإبلاغهما ما أمرهما الله أن يقولا لفرعون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rather than engage Moses' message, Pharaoh invokes his family's upbringing of him and the killing, hoping to extinguish the mission and frighten Moses into silence under color of justified punishment.
rows.anchor: فعدل إلى تذكيره بنعمة الفراعنة أسلافه على موسى وتخويفه من جنايته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question presses Moses to acknowledge the upbringing, despite being phrased around its denial; Pharaoh presents acknowledgment as voluntary and free of fear or coercion.
rows.anchor: على نفي التربية مع أن المقصود الإقرار بوقوع التربية مجاراة لحال موسى في نظر فرعون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Ashur also allows a reproachful question: Pharaoh treats Moses as if he denied being raised among them or thought they had forgotten his deed; either way he casts Moses as a denier.
rows.anchor: أن يجعل الاستفهام إنكاريا عليه لأن لسان حال موسى في نظر فرعون حال من يجحد أنه مربى فيهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: التربية means taking charge of a child's care and affairs; فينا means in the royal Egyptian household, and وليد means a newborn or very young child.
rows.anchor: والتربية : كفالة الصبي وتدبير شؤونه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh refers to Moses being taken from the Nile and raised in the royal household.
rows.anchor: يعني بذلك التقاطه من نهر النيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Ashur identifies Moses' foster father as Ramses II of Egypt's nineteenth dynasty and the Pharaoh confronted by Moses as Merneptah II, his son and successor; Moses may have been raised with him like a brother.
rows.anchor: من ملوك العائلة التاسعة عشرة من عائلات فراعنة مصر

rows.speaker: التوراة
rows.claim: The source says Moses left Egypt at about forty after killing the Egyptian, and was commissioned at eighty, citing the Torah for the latter age.
rows.anchor: وبعث وعمره ثمانون سنة حسبما في التوراة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: فعلة is a single occurrence of an act; here, by its attachment to the addressee, it denotes the result of the act, the killing of the Egyptian.
rows.anchor: وأراد بها الحاصل بالمصدر كما اقتضته إضافتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The deed is Moses' killing of the Copt; Pharaoh calls it by a relative expression because Moses knows which deed, using that reference to reproach him.
rows.anchor: بالفعلة قتله القبطي ، قيل هو

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: An unnamed reported view identifies the slain Copt as Pharaoh's baker.
rows.anchor: القبطي ، قيل هو خباز فرعون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The vague, repetitive naming magnifies the deed as notorious and makes Pharaoh's attribution of responsibility to Moses seem inescapable.
rows.anchor: عن ذكر فعلة معينة إلى ذكرها مبهمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause وأنت من الكافرين is a circumstantial clause attached to the subject of فعلت.
rows.anchor: حال من ضمير { فعلت }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here Pharaoh means ingratitude for the royal upbringing: Moses defended an Israelite whom Pharaoh's people treated as a slave, rather than identifying with Pharaoh's household; this reverses lineage and adoption.
rows.anchor: والمراد به كفر نعمة فرعون من حيث اعتدى على أحد خاصته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The accusation is not unbelief in Pharaoh's religion at the time of the killing: Moses had not openly opposed that faith, though inwardly he did, and prophets are protected from unbelief before and after prophethood.
rows.anchor: لأن موسى لم يكن يوم قتل القبطي متظاهرا بأنه على خلاف دينهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, this may be a coordinated reproach: Pharaoh accuses Moses of currently disbelieving their religion, since the active participle denotes the present state.
rows.anchor: عطفا على الجمل التي قبلها التي هي توبيخ ولوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further possibility is that Pharaoh means Moses was already an unbeliever in their religion at the time, inferred from signs of contempt for their faith and its loyalty to Pharaoh.
rows.anchor: وأنت حينئذ من الكافرين بديننا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses lived among Pharaoh's people for about forty years.
rows.anchor: والسنين التي لبثها موسى فيهم هي نحو أربعين سنة
